sense.text:
Everything about the Bible is a secret, and the churches do not know the secrets, or they would not be calling themselves Methodist, Baptist, Catholic, Jehovah’s Witness, 7th Day Adventist, Protestant or Lutheran. None of that is in the Bible. Here God brought the Israelites into a covenant and made a deal with them.

“If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God”: that is what this ministry tries to get our people to do. Not to hearken to us, not to a pastor telling you this is your season, because the Lord determines that, but to the voice of the Lord thy God, “to observe and to do all his commandments.” That is why people can’t stand that we keep teaching God’s commandments.

The promise: “the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth.” God wanted one nation, the 12 tribes of Israel, to be above all nations of the earth.
“And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee.” Listen to the law, the statutes and the commandments of God, and you will be a blessed people.

“Blessed shalt thou be in the city”: that is what we want. We are tired of being in the ghettos, the hood and the slums, eating crumbs.

“And blessed shalt thou be in the field”: we want the fields to bring forth everything we need, not to have to go to a supermarket for GMO foods and fake artificial foods. We do not own the food manufacturing plants; they used us in the fields for slave labor.

“Blessed shall be the fruit of thy body”: we want to be healthy, when we can’t afford health care and have been experimented on by mad scientists and doctors who make us sick and then inject drugs into us. “The fruit of thy ground”: good things coming from the ground. “The fruit of thy cattle”: you can’t even drink the milk here or eat the cattle, because they force-feed the animals to make them big and inject them with antibiotics, so we are eating sick cattle. “The flocks of thy sheep”: they stole our sheep from us.
“Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store”: our finances. It was all taken from us because we did not keep this covenant, as verse 15 shows.

“If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God”: and we didn’t. We did not listen to him; we broke the covenant. So “all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.” People say, I’m not cursed, I ain’t under no curse. The Lord made good on his promise.

“Cursed shalt thou be in the city”: that is why we are in the ghettos and the slums, called bums and given crumbs, while they live in neighborhoods exclusive to them that we can’t afford to live in.

They say black people kill each other, but this is the result of systematic oppression: flooding our cities with drugs and guns, restricting our jobs and our education, making it hard for the black man to stand in his household, and then complaining about how we treat each other. When we tried to build our cities up, like Tulsa, Oklahoma, pulling ourselves up by our bootstraps, they set the city on fire and burned it down. There has always been a system in place to destroy us based on our race: the Ku Klux Klan, the courts, law enforcement, the Tuskegee experiment, Flint, Michigan, the media and the music. And now they are erasing our history, shredding the old books and pricing them out of our reach, so that we cannot teach who are the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

During slavery they made it illegal for us to read, then mocked us: if you want to hide something from a black person, put it in a book. Now that we are reading, we are finding everything they hid. But the one book they don’t want us to look in is the Bible, and the mysteries of God.

This comes after God brought us into a covenant, and it is a warning: “Lest there should be among you man, or woman, or family, or tribe, whose heart turneth away this day from the Lord our God.” The Lord wants our heart aligned with his heart.

“To go and serve the gods of these nations”: like you see right now. Methodist, Baptist, Catholic, Jehovah’s Witness, 7th Day Adventist: God didn’t give you that. Those are gods manufactured by these nations, and they cannot give you salvation.

“That he bless himself in his heart, saying, I shall have peace, though I walk in the imagination of mine heart”: that is what our people think, that they can make things up and still have peace. That is why they give you a feel-good religion, a white Jesus that loves everybody and died for everybody, to pull you away from God’s mission of keeping the covenant as the 12 tribes of Israel; contrary to the Jesus of the Bible, who died exclusively for the 12 tribes of Israel.

“To add drunkenness to thirst”: we are thirsty for knowledge of the Most High, and our people are moving like drunkards.

“The anger of the Lord and his jealousy shall smoke against that man.” When we turn against the Lord he gets angry and jealous, because he set us up to be his representatives on this earth. “All the curses that are written in this book shall lie upon him”: we lose our land, our heritage, our culture, our identity, and face death. He brought us to reform and restructure this earth; when we go against him we make him look bad. “The Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven”: God gave you life and you bring him strife.

“The Lord shall separate him unto evil out of all the tribes of Israel.” That is why bad things happen to us: God cuts us off from his nation. That is why in Hosea he said, You are not my people, and pushed the Israelites among the Gentiles, and why Paul in the New Testament calls them Gentiles and speaks of salvation to the Gentiles. The Israelites were split into two kingdoms, Judah and Israel; God cut off the northern kingdom, and in the New Testament they are called heathen, uncircumcised, Gentiles, idolaters. The religions of man will not teach you that history.

“The generation to come of your children that shall rise up after you, and the stranger that shall come from a far land”: after we were cut off, a new generation pops up, and the other nations see “the plagues of that land”: us destroyed, living in the hood, the ghettos and the slums, with another nation ruling over us. “And the sicknesses which the Lord hath laid upon it”: we are not healthy, mentally or physically.

“Brimstone, and salt, and burning”, then “like the overthrow of Sodom, and Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim.” The Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah because they were sexually immoral, and that is what they train us to be now: not honoring marriage, homosexuality pushed, young children having sex instead of growing into decent women and respectable men. When the Lord doesn’t like how you’re living, he stops giving you life and you get death.

This is also a secret being revealed to us. Deuteronomy 28 ends with us going into Egypt again in ships, and that Egypt is America, spiritual Egypt. So chapter 29 is us here in America, and verse 23 is the judgment to come here: the whole land “brimstone, and salt, and burning, that it is not sown, nor beareth, nor any grass groweth therein.” Our people here who will not repent when they hear the word, the Lord will destroy, and this place will be destroyed with brimstone and fire, just as he destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. No church will teach this.

“Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land? what meaneth the heat of this great anger?” That is what people ask when we tell them we are the Israelites, the ones under the curse, the ones on the bottom, who lost our land, heritage and identity. Now we are called American, after an Italian explorer; African, after a Roman conqueror, Scipio Africanus; West Indian, Puerto Rican, Haitian, Dominican, Indian. We lost our name, and lost our fame with the most high God.

“Because they have forsaken the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers.” A new generation will ask why things are so bad for these people, and this is the answer. We were brought into a covenant to establish a government, we broke that covenant, and now we are at the bottom. “When he brought them forth out of the land of Egypt”: he took us out of bondage and said, I’m going to free you and make you great.

“For they went and served other gods, and worshipped them, gods whom they knew not.” God took us out of the worst slavery, beaten and worked from sun up to sun down, and we turned our back on him. Use logic: if a God delivered you and changed your life, drowned the Egyptians’ army and killed their firstborn, promised you would rule the earth, and you gave him the finger and went to worship another god, and he did nothing, in the street we would call him a sucker. So everything he did to us is justified. Our people are evil; they got the devil on them.

“To bring upon it all the curses that are written in this book”: because he warned us in Deuteronomy 28. If he did not put us in captivity and punish us, he would be a liar. Where we grew up they said, My name is my bond; you ain’t going to throw dirt on my name. It’s the same with the most high God: you ain’t going to throw dirt on his name and think it’s a game.

“The Lord rooted them out of their land in anger, and in wrath, and in great indignation, and cast them into another land.” That is why black people went into captivity on slave ships from Africa to North and Central America, to the islands of the West Indies and all the other places on the earth, as Moses warned. We are scattered all over the earth because we didn’t understand our worth, and the Bible now is bringing us back to God, back into the covenant, to establish God’s government.

“As it is this day”: to this day we are the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The churches don’t start from the beginning of the Bible and give you the history: freedom from the Egyptians, enslavement by the Babylonians, the Assyrians, the Persians and the Medes, the Greeks, then Rome, then the savior God promised, whom the Roman government and the leaders of the church cried out to crucify.

“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever.” That is who this Bible is for. God is not going to give these secrets to the other nations; they belong to us now and to our children who come after us. Shame on you parents who don’t sit down and teach your children this biblical history and connect them back to the father, but let TV and the American education system raise them. If your kid doesn’t want to read the Bible, make him read it like you make him do his homework; if he won’t read, sit him in front of a class. And shame on the wife who will support her husband to go to the concert but gets screw-face mad when he asks her to listen to a class.

“That we may do all the words of this law”: that is what the secrets are for.

Everything just read was a secret: chapter 29 is us here in America, spiritual Egypt, and the judgment coming on it. It is the secret that belongs to the Lord, and it is being revealed unto us today.

precepts.why:
No church is teaching that God brought the chosen people into a covenant, that they would break it, and that God would get angry and scatter them to the four corners of the earth. “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.” God would not be God if he had just left us alone after we broke the covenant. Black people ask, What type of God would do that? That’s an evil God. You didn’t want to follow him when he revealed himself to you the first time.

We were in one geographic location as a powerful nation. The reason we are scattered all over is our disobedience: he said he would scatter us from one end of the earth to the other. That is how he “cast them into another land.”

“And there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known”: Methodist, Catholic, Jehovah’s Witness, Lutheran, Mormon, Pentecostal, apologist, each a different god with nothing to do with the Bible. We never heard of a white Jesus until they manufactured him in the Renaissance, when Pope Alexander VI, Rodrigo Borgia, had his son Cesare’s image painted as Jesus Christ, and now black people wear a white imaginary man around their neck and hang his picture on the wall.

“Even wood and stone”: the wooden cross with the white image of Jesus Christ, and the stone that the Arabs made us bow to at Zanzibar, the biggest slave port. That is why black men go to prison and come out Muslim, not knowing that the same Arabs who enslaved and renamed them gave them that religion, from a book that came 600 years after the Bible was complete. If we are wrong, come and show us: but we want book, chapter and verse, not your religious doctrine you rehearse.

This Bible is a secret only for us. God never gave it to the whole world; the only reason the whole world has it is that they took it from us in captivity. This is our book.

“He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” Unto who? Israel. This was only for the Israelites.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them.” God did not show these secrets to the other nations. What is written in the Bible, the judgments, they don’t know, because God never brought them into a covenant. So the things revealed belong to Israel and to their children, and to no one else.

“And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else.” Where is God? In the midst of Israel. The God of this Bible is exclusive to us, and none else.

“And my people shall never be ashamed.” We are ashamed because they erased our name: black, African, Negro, Caribbean, American, West Indian. You come to America for citizenship because you are ashamed of where you came from and want to be Americanized, because they have everything you lost when the curses came on you. There is a God who can give it back, but you have to return to him.

“I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.” The Most High is putting his spirit on us, and we will prophesy, because the Bible is a book of prophecy; religion the white man gave you cannot save you. “Your old men shall dream dreams”: many of you were having bad dreams, and it all made sense when you came into this truth.

“The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood”: the sun and moon represent wisdom; looking into prophecy, we see destruction coming, “before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.” Is the church telling you a great and terrible day is coming, or that God is good all the time and to sow a $1,000 seed? This is a secret, and only we can speak it.

sense.text:
“Against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth.” They get mad when we point that out. God didn’t deal with the other families of the earth. If God was for everybody, why put only the Israelites in an exclusive covenant?

“Therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.” That is why things are the way they are. A real God makes good on his claim.
“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” You have to be in agreement with your God; you are not walking with him if you don’t agree with him.
The lion roaring with prey, the young lion crying out of his den, the bird falling in the snare, the snare taken up: cause and effect. There is a cause and an effect for everything.

“Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?” The trumpet declares that war is coming, and the trumpet now is the Bible. As we ring the alarm, you are supposed to be afraid of what is written, not sitting in church listening to lies and paying tithes to a pastor who can’t open your eyes.

“Shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” The evil done to the Israelites is because they went against the Lord. The evil you see now, the United States attacking countries and bombing places, the world at war: the Lord already wrote it, nation shall rise against nation.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” While there is evil going on, God reveals his secrets to those who serve him. The Israelites are his servants, the ones called to serve him. And the prophets: we are the ministry that goes into the Bible and prophesies, while the Christian church gives theology and prosperity teaching. As God brings this evil on the city, he has put the spirit on us to prophesy.
“The Lord God hath spoken, who can but prophesy?” All we have to do when we read the prophecy is prophesy. These are God’s words.

“Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt”, then “the oppressed in the midst thereof”: we are the oppressed in these lands. Those in Samaria were Israelites; the good Samaritan was an Israelite of the northern kingdom. So publish these things in the lands of our captivity, “for they know not to do right”: our people don’t know right from wrong, and glorify violence and robbery in another man’s land.

“An adversary there shall be even round about the land; and he shall bring down thy strength from thee”: the Lord used the other nations to bring us down. As a shepherd takes out of the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, “so shall the children of Israel be taken out.”

“Hear ye, and testify in the house of Jacob”: we have to testify to our people about what went wrong, and give them the word of God to make them strong. When God visits the transgressions of Israel he cuts off everything we believed in, the altars and their horns, and smites the winter house and the summer house, because destruction is coming while we are comfortable disregarding God’s secrets and living a life of evil.

This is how secrets get revealed to us. Job was going back and forth with his friends, and Zophar told him not to think he was better than God. “When thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?” When you say something stupid concerning God, there should be men of God there to check you.
“My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes”: Job was acting like he had done nothing wrong.

“But oh that God would speak”, then “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom.” In our minds we believe we are not wrong and don’t deserve what God is doing to us, so Zophar wished God would come to Job personally and show him, because he was trying to justify himself.

“That they are double to that which is”: the things written are twofold, more than what you think is right there. As was just brought out in Deuteronomy, Moses was warning them in his day, and the same words are the future prophecy of the United States of America, spiritual Egypt, made uninhabitable. That is double meaning.

“Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.” Whatever we complain about, we could be dead. After we gave God the finger, he is taking it easy on us. Job lost his servants, his children died, his wife told him to curse God and die, and his friend still told him God went easy on him. Ponder how merciful he is.

“Canst thou by searching find out God?” You can’t find out his perfection no matter how long you sit down. What we learned, the white man didn’t teach us: they don’t know the Bible, and they are afraid of what we are learning, because the secret things belong to us. They took the Bible from us and weren’t smart enough to get rid of it. “If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?” Nobody can stop God; how dare you question him.

“He seeth wickedness also.” Before this truth you ate ham hocks, shrimp, crab, pork and lobster, and lived in adultery, and felt nothing was wrong, until you read the word of God and understood why it is evil.

“If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him”: that is what we are doing. “If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away”: stop sinning, which is what this ministry teaches; that is why we take you through the commandments. People call us strict; we are telling you how to understand the secrets of God and get closer to him. “Let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles”: not in the body, not in the place of fellowship. The churches are dumb because they allow wickedness in the place where they are supposed to commune with God.

“Then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot”: Here I am, God; I learned thou shalt not kill, steal or commit adultery. You won’t fear, because you are not doing anything wicked. Walking in righteousness brings the Lord to your side, and that is how God reveals mysteries to you. You cannot be evil and stand before God as his people.
“Thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning”: wisdom is a light, Jesus Christ is the light, and we are to be like it.

Because we cleansed our heart, got rid of the spot and opened our hands, “thou shalt take thy rest in safety”, then “thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid.” We are afraid now because another nation rules over us, since we sinned: the police pulling us over, losing our job, food and gas prices. Come close to God with no spot and no blemish and we can lie down and relax.

“But the eyes of the wicked shall fail”: God will not reveal the secrets to them. “Their hope shall be as the giving up of the ghost”: their hope is just to die. It is a secret to them that by keeping God’s commandments you can have everlasting life, and that if we die before the great day of judgment God will resurrect our spirit. The church doesn’t teach that.

“Many are in high place, and of renown”: people in powerful positions, high government, celebrities, athletes. “But mysteries are revealed unto the meek.” The meek of the earth are the Israelites; the mysteries of God have been revealed unto us.

“Seek not out the things that are too hard for thee”, then “But what is commanded thee, think thereupon with reverence.” He commanded us to keep the commandments and keep his covenant, and he will give us everything else and put us high above all nations of the earth. “It is not needful for thee to see with thine eyes the things that are in secret”: some things God keeps to himself. That is why some of you are into tarot cards, brujería, Changó, voodoo, wanting to see secret spiritual things. All you have to do is keep the commandments.

“Be not curious in unnecessary matters”: like Eve in the garden. She was already in paradise, and Satan whispered in her ear, and she became curious: maybe God lied to us, maybe there’s better than this. “More things are shewed unto thee than men understand”: we don’t even understand what we see with our eyes. That is why the Illuminati and secret societies don’t matter; they will burn when we get our turn, and the Bible is the only thing we are supposed to learn.

“Many are deceived by their own vain opinion”: deviating from what is written. “And an evil suspicion hath overthrown their judgment”: Eve had an evil suspicion of God when Satan told her her eyes would be opened. “Profess not the knowledge therefore that thou hast not”: Satan brought her knowledge she didn’t need. All she had to do was obey.

“A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last”: refuse to keep the commandments and evil comes to your doorstep. “He that loveth danger shall perish therein”: some of you like the life you are living, adultery, alcohol, drugs. “An obstinate heart shall be laden with sorrows”: your life is sorrow because your heart is obstinate against God. “In the punishment of the proud there is no remedy; for the plant of wickedness hath taken root in him”: God sowed a righteous seed, Satan sowed a wicked seed, and when it takes root, all the punishment and captivity are no benefit to you.
“The heart of the prudent will understand a parable”: the parables are mysteries, and the prudent heart discerns them.

“Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms maketh an atonement for sins.” Alms is assistance for your people, for the poor; when Israel collected alms it was for the healing and the building of the nation, not for a pastor’s Bentley, mansion and jet-set life. As water puts out a fire, alms given to the right people, people not in evil, make an atonement for sin; God sees you have mercy in your heart. That is a mystery the church doesn’t know. If you miss a month of alms, double up the next.

“He that requiteth good turns is mindful of that which may come hereafter”: there is cause and effect in giving. “When he falleth, he shall find a stay”: like Manasses, who did much evil but still helped his people, and the Lord delivered him.

When we say the Bible is exclusive to the Israelites, the heathen and the Gentiles always bring up Rahab the harlot, because the New Testament mentions her faith. They never say why. Joshua sent two men “to spy secretly”, and they came into an harlot’s house, named Rahab, because they were going to take the land.
Somebody saw the two men, foreigners searching out the land, and the king of Jericho demanded that Rahab bring them forth.

“And the woman took the two men, and hid them”: listen to why. She told the king’s men she didn’t know where they were from or where they went: she lied to her own people. She hid them on the roof “with the stalks of flax” while the pursuers ran toward Jordan.

“I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us”: everybody was afraid of the Israelites. That is why she hid them. They heard how the Lord dried up the Red sea, what he did to the Egyptians, and to the two kings of the Amorites, Sihon and Og: “our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man.” She knew they had a real God, “God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.”

“Since I have shewed you kindness, that ye will also shew kindness unto my father’s house”: don’t kill me and my family. That is all it was about. Based on what she saw of the God of Israel, she knew it could happen to her, so she made a deal: I won’t tell my people where you are if you spare me. That was the faith of Rahab: that if she went on the mercy of these Israelite men, they would spare her. Our own people won’t ask the Lord for mercy, but this heathen woman, seeing the works of the Lord, would see her whole city killed to spare her house.
“Our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business”: we won’t wipe your whole family out.

“We will be blameless of this thine oath”: if anything goes wrong, don’t blame us. The scarlet thread in the window told the army to leave that house alone; she was the one who helped them. Bring all the family into the house, because every house was about to be torn up, and whoever stepped out into the street, “his blood shall be upon his head.”

“Truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land; for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us.” She told them the reason they would win is that everybody was afraid, and she kept it a secret. People bring her up to say there is salvation for her nation, but all of them were wiped out. The Lord spared her house because she helped the Israelites. So to the heathen and Gentiles watching who ask what they can do: do like Rahab did. Hold us down so you can spare your town.

precepts.why:
These are examples of the secrets of the Most High. The Lord told Abram, “I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great.”

“And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee.” That is why Rahab was read. People say this God just wants to kill everybody. No: if you are on our side, you can come along for the ride. He blesses them that bless Israel and curses them that curse Israel, and some of you think you will curse us and get away with it with no consequences.

So one who finds out they are not an Israelite can say, this worked for Rahab; let me help them, and the Lord will have mercy on me.

sense.text: “And the Lord appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre”, and then “three men stood by him.” It was not physically the most high God or the Messiah; the Lord can appear as men. People don’t understand the secrets of how the scriptures are written. There was something spiritual about these men, so when Abraham saw them he bowed himself toward the ground.

“My Lord, if now I have found favour in thy sight”: he called those three men my Lord, and begged them to come to his house, wash their feet and rest. He told Sarah to make ready quickly three measures of fine meal, ran to the herd for a calf tender and good, and set it before them with butter and milk. These were men of the Lord.

“Sarah thy wife shall have a son.” Sarah was in the tent door behind him, eavesdropping; they weren’t talking to her. Abraham and Sarah were nearly a hundred years old, and it had ceased to be with her after the manner of women, so she laughed within herself, not out loud: “After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?”

In her head she was saying, my old vagina is going to bring a baby? What the hell are they talking about? He’s old too; we ain’t done it in a long time.

Abraham was a hundred and still getting it in, still having kids at 120, and his wife still looked good at that age: they still had the desire for each other. Some of you are 40, 50 and have to pop a pill, or 35, 40 and say, we don’t do it anymore. In the beginning of the relationship he slaps her butt while she washes the dishes; now he walks by and doesn’t even look. Abraham was still slapping that booty at 120. We are real far behind.

“Wherefore did Sarah laugh?” She only laughed within herself, and they knew it. She was outside the tent not minding her damn business, and the men told Abraham, check your wife. “Is any thing too hard for the Lord?”

“Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not; for she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh.” So she did laugh; that’s how we know she was black. Why did she lie? Because of fear, like a child who says no when asked, did you do that, because he is scared of a whooping. Lying is wrong, but there is a lie out of fear, and there is the lie that is dangerous: the lie told to deceive and destroy, like someone saying a person touched them when the cameras show he was never near her. That is a wicked, despicable woman; a seed of evil has been planted inside of her. Sarah’s lie was out of fear.

The Lord came to tell Abraham a child would be born at a hundred years old, but then: “Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do?” Destruction was coming, and nobody knew it. Should we tell Abraham? Should we let him in on the secret?

“For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him.” The Lord said, you can tell him; he is righteous, I know him, he keeps his house in order and won’t let wickedness into it. That is why we are the way we are with your families. How many of you can say God knows you, and that secrets should be revealed to you based on your walk and how you talk?
“Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous; I will go down now, and see.”

The men went toward Sodom, “but Abraham stood yet before the Lord” and asked, “Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?” They didn’t tell him everybody would be wiped out, and he thought there were righteous people in the city. It is the same with us now: we don’t know who is keeping the commandments and who is in wickedness. Abraham thought there were righteous there, and there were none.

“If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sakes.” Abraham kept lowering the number, forty and five, forty, thirty, twenty, ten, and the Lord said, “I will not destroy it for ten’s sake.”

precepts.why:
This is when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and the Bible keeps making reference to it. “The burden of Babylon”: the Lord sent Isaiah a vision. “Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain”: the banner is the Bible, the mountain the governments. “Exalt the voice unto them, shake the hand”: as we do, raising our voice to the people with the word of God and telling them how wicked they are. “I have commanded my sanctified ones”: we have been sanctified with the word. “I have also called my mighty ones”: the angels. God is angry, and “the Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle”, gathering all the nations to destroy them.

“And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” He burned that place up. America is modern-day Babylon, and America is going to get burned up when God turns it up, and they are clueless. There was an ancient Babylon taken by the Persians and the Medes; now there is a spiritual Babylon that will be just like Sodom and Gomorrah.

“It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation”, then “But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there.” America will be uninhabitable. That is the secret we understand.

Christ makes mention of it too. “See here; or, see there: go not after them”: the religious denominations lead you down different paths to find Christ. We know he is the black Messiah who will set this earth on fire. “But first must he suffer many things, and be rejected of this generation”: he came to his own and his own received him not; the leaders of the church worked with the Roman government against him.

“As it was in the days of Noe”, then “They did eat, they drank, they married wives”: clueless until the flood came. “Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot”, then “the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven.” The Most High did not broadcast that he would destroy Sodom and Gomorrah. He told only Abraham, because he knew him. Lot did not find out until the day itself, when the angels came and got him out because he was Abraham’s nephew; he had no time to prepare and had to leave everything. Abraham got advance information and learned God’s secret.

“Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.” The Lord is letting us into his secret in advance: America is Babylon and it will be burned. Does the rest of the world know a nuclear war is coming and billions will die? “Remember Lot’s wife”: she wasn’t prepared. Like the movie House of Dynamite, where people had minutes, not hours, there will be no time to call your mother or your auntie. “Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it”: this life in Babylon, America, is temporary; don’t hold on to it.

Being an Israelite is not enough. Two thirds will be destroyed and only one third pulled through the fire, so ask: how do I comply so I don’t die? “The one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.” Only a select group will know, and they will know when it’s time to go. This is the biggest secret on the earth, and y’all take this ministry for a joke.

“Where, Lord?”, then “Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together.” Revelation speaks of a great feast to clean up the dead: that is America, which will get all the nukes and be uninhabitable. These are the secrets the Most High is revealing to us.

sense.text:
“There were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you”: like these lying churches, Methodist, Baptist, Jehovah’s Witness, 7th Day Adventist, apologists. They don’t know the Bible, they don’t talk prophecy, and they can’t see that the God of this Bible is angry and is going to destroy people. They argue about whether the Gentiles will be saved, when you don’t know if you’re going to be saved yourself. You’re worried about them, and your ass is going to get burned up when God turns it up.

“Damnable heresies”: making things up that don’t line up with scripture, and getting people damned. “Denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction”: Christ died for the 12 tribes of Israel, and that is a mystery the other ministries don’t know.

“Many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of.” The truth, the laws of God and what is in prophecy, they will speak evil of. Give them book, chapter and verse and they will hold on to what they rehearse, because God put them under a curse. They will not get the secrets of the most high God.

“Through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you”: everything going to be all right, God is good all the time. They make you suckers: every Sunday you give away your money. “Whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not”: judgment has been waiting on them a long time, and God is going to kick that ass.

“God spared not the angels that sinned”, then “And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness.” Noah was saved because he taught the people how to behave, the same thing we are doing now. His house was spared while the rest watched him build an ark, because they were not righteous like Noah.

precepts.why:
They were not righteous like Noah. “The sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose”: they lusted after the women. “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh”: when we go against God’s spirit, he causes strife; in the flesh we do what feels best instead of following the Most High’s instructions. “Yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years”: God cut our lifespan short; before that men lived 500, 600, 700 years, and Methuselah over 900.

“Every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually”, then “But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” Noah was exceptional: “a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God”, keeping the commandments. Today we tell people to keep the laws and they call us legalists.

“The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.” We touch on the days of Noah, marrying and giving in marriage, but we fail to put emphasis on the violence. There were wars and killing all over the earth then, Cain and his descendants, and the same is happening today. The Lord said, these people are too violent, I have to wipe them out, and it will be the same in these last days: if the Lord doesn’t intervene, the white man will destroy everything on the earth. Because of the blood being shed on the earth by Esau, the so-called white man, the Lord will intervene again and destroy that civilization, this time with fire.

“Make thee an ark of gopher wood.” Why did he only tell Noah to build the ark, and not everybody else? The same with Abraham: only he was told destruction was coming. The Lord kept it a secret, and what we know is a secret the churches don’t know. When these things are revealed to you as you read, it is because of your godly character. You are in an exclusive place to get God’s grace.

sense.text: The same thing that happened with Abraham happened with Lot: two angels came, and Lot rose up and bowed himself with his face toward the ground. Real recognized real: Lot knew who they were, as Abraham did. He pressed upon them greatly, brought them in and made them a feast.

“The men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter”, saying, “bring them out unto us, that we may know them.” They watched who came into the man of God’s house and wanted to rape the angels. That batty boy spirit, that sodomite spirit, is alive again here in America. You hear of women being raped; you will start to hear of men being raped. So brothers, work out and get your muscles up. And that ain’t no regular batty boy; that’s a gangster batty boy, the violent one, the homo thugs that come out of prison where they raped dudes, on the street doing the same thing. They will kill you and take it. The churches won’t point it out, and they call us evil for explaining it.

“I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly”, and Lot offered his two daughters which had not known man; they said, we don’t want no vagina. “Now will we deal worse with thee, than with them”: that is how sick that spirit is. Those people are not normal; there is something behind it, a level of violence and aggression, because God did not design man for that. They pressed sore on Lot and came near to break the door: ready to break the door for booty.

The angels pulled Lot in and smote the men with blindness, “so that they wearied themselves to find the door.” Even blind they would not go home; something is mentally wrong with you to go after men that bad.

“We will destroy this place, because the cry of them is waxen great.” Lot told his sons in law, “Up, get you out of this place”, “but he seemed as one that mocked unto his sons in law.” Some in your own house will not see what you see spiritually and will not take you seriously; don’t assume everybody is as spiritual as you are.
“And while he lingered”: Lot was taking his time, and the men laid hold on his hand and his wife’s and his daughters’, “the Lord being merciful unto him”, and set him outside the city.

“Escape for thy life; look not behind thee.” Lot asked to flee to the little city near by, and was granted it: “I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither.” Again, exclusive information for his salvation: get your wife and daughters and go. He didn’t warn anybody else in the city. That is how the Lord works. We know today this place is going to be destroyed for the same things as in Noah’s time and in Lot’s city. You are in a secret place of the Most High, and that is a beautiful place to be, so don’t take this Bible or this ministry for a joke.

Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman he married; it was in the law not to be with the heathen. “Hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?” They thought they were on the same level as Moses.
“Now the man Moses was very meek”: whatever God said to do, he did. Moses did not go against God.

“If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream. My servant Moses is not so.” I don’t deal with Moses the way I deal with you. “With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches.” Moses was in an exclusive place with him.

“And the anger of the Lord was kindled against them.” Miriam was struck with leprosy. Moses was given exclusive information, and Aaron and his sister were on the sideline acting like they were equal. It is the same with the Israelite camps: the Lord isn’t dealing with them all the same. Some he reveals information to; others only know they are Israelites and understand no prophecy, and the denominations know nothing spiritual about the Bible. Now they challenge us, because the Most High blessed our teachers and leaders and showed us the secrets of the Bible.
“The word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision”: the priests were not seeing visions. Eli’s eyes began to wax dim.

The Lord called Samuel three times, and each time he ran to Eli, until Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child: the Most High was dealing with him. Hannah had sent him to the priest in priestly clothing as a little child, and it took a while in the priesthood before God dealt with him directly, in an exclusive place, as he did with Moses. “Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth.”

“I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle.” He had warned Eli that his sons were wicked, and now he told Samuel he was about to destroy Eli’s house. “For I have told him”: the Lord had already spoken to Eli.

“For the iniquity which he knoweth”: not iniquity Eli did, but iniquity he knew of. Eli was not a wicked man; his sons “made themselves vile”, he knew it, and God told him to check his sons, but he turned a blind eye. That is why the Lord judged him.

“And he restrained them not.” Many of you are weak with your kids and will let them destroy your house. When we see things spiritually and tell you, your son ain’t right, your daughter ain’t right, your wife ain’t right, you should listen, not overlook it like Eli as if you can’t get touched.
“The iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever”: no offering, no sacrifice; your life has to pay.

Samuel “feared to shew Eli the vision”, but Eli made him tell every whit, and said, “It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good.” He was ready to die rather than correct his children. Hearing from another priest that God was about to tear his house up, he should have corrected his sons that day: an exclusive ass whooping, with their mother trying to stop him and people saying he lost his damn mind. The Most High will deal with men exclusively, in a place where he doesn’t deal with others the same way.

Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams “wherewith his spirit was troubled”, and called the magicians, astrologers, sorcerers and Chaldeans, but “The thing is gone from me”: he did not remember the dream, and said if they could not tell it with the interpretation they would be cut in pieces. Dreams can trouble you for days, when you can’t remember who was leading you somewhere. He knew they were only trying to “gain the time.”

The decree went forth to slay the wise men, and they sought Daniel and his fellows. Daniel answered “with counsel and wisdom”: “Why is the decree so hasty from the king?” Slow down; let me go talk to God.
Daniel told Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, “That they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret.” Let’s ask God to reveal it to us.
“Then was the secret revealed unto Daniel in a night vision”, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven, who “removeth kings, and setteth up kings.”

The great image: head of fine gold, breast and arms of silver, belly and thighs of brass, legs of iron, feet part iron and part clay, and the stone cut out without hands. He was seeing the empires of the world: the Babylonians, the Persians and the Medes, the Greeks, and Rome.
“The great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter”: the rise and fall of empires. “The dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.”

The king fell on his face and said, “your God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets.” It is a good thing to have someone who can recall your dream and tell you the secret, the vision shown to you.

Because he could reveal the secret, the king made Daniel ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and Daniel set Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego over its affairs: he set his men up. It is good when the Lord reveals secrets to you, especially to interpret a dream.

Look what the Lord said about Ezra: “Thou only hast been meet to know this secret of the Highest.” “Write all these things that thou hast seen in a book, and hide them: And teach them to the wise of the people, whose hearts thou knowest may comprehend and keep these secrets.” The Lord shows exclusive information to teachers, and they give it to the others who are worthy.

precepts.why: The Lord told Ezra the information he showed him was exclusive, not to give to everybody: “some things shalt thou publish, and some things shalt thou shew secretly to the wise.” These are the secrets of the Most High. Everybody is not going to know everything we know, and that is how the Lord wants it.

sense.text: Hezekiah as king “had done the thing that pleased the Lord”, and Isaiah the prophet was with him, “great and faithful in his vision.” In his time the sun went backward and the king’s life was lengthened.

“He saw by an excellent spirit what should come to pass at the last, and he comforted them that mourned in Sion. He shewed what should come to pass for ever, and secret things or ever they came.” That is what a true prophet does: comfort the people that mourn and explain to them the secret things. No ministry is doing what we do, going into the Bible and showing secret things while the world is falling apart.
“And he spake many things unto them in parables”, so much that his disciples began to question him.

“Why speakest thou unto them in parables?”, then “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” This Bible, this understanding, is not for everybody. You are in an exclusive place to receive God’s grace.

It was prophesied that Christ would speak in parables: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.” These secrets are being revealed to us. We understand the parables; we understand destruction is coming.

precepts.why:
Where was it written? “Give ear, O my people, to my law”, then “I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old”, which is what Christ did.

“We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come.” The generation to come needs to understand this Bible. The Lord revealed it to this generation, and the secret is that destruction is coming and we are the Israelites; we are not to hide it from our children. “For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel”: the testimony is you are in a covenant with me as my chosen people.

“That the generation to come might know them, even the children which should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children.” We went into captivity because we weren’t keeping the laws; now a new generation is being taught them. Children married the way the scriptures say, who never ate shrimp, crab, pork or lobster, never put a razor to their face, never gave their virginity away, never celebrated Christmas or Halloween. The Most High waited to reveal this secret to this generation so that your children could bring forth a righteous nation the world has never seen.

“That they might set their hope in God, and not forget the works of God”, then “And might not be as their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation.” We know where things went wrong, so we can raise a new generation that is strong. You won’t learn that in any church.

“With many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it.” Christ always spoke in parables. “And when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.” He knew most of the people could not understand, but alone with his disciples he explained it.

That is why we get on you men who stay off to the side when we are together. The bishop is dropping gems, the deacons are dropping gems, expounding things most people don’t know. When you have time alone with the bishops and the deacons, embrace it, as the disciples did with Christ.

sense.text: “To stablish you according to my gospel, and the preaching of Jesus Christ”: we are established to understand that Jesus Christ, the black Messiah, died to save us from our sin. “According to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began.” People don’t know this: we were the first to tell you Christ died exclusively for the Israelites, and that you must keep the commandments to show you love him. Everything we teach was a secret since the world began, and now the Most High is revealing his plan.

“But now is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets”, then “made known to all nations for the obedience of faith.” The Lord put the spirit on us to preach, and we go throughout the world to all nations, telling them of the Israelites, the 12 tribes, doing what Christ said: go find the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and as you go, preach the kingdom. No other ministry is teaching that.

“Not with excellency of speech or of wisdom”: not like the Christian church, speaking all proper with big words. “Save Jesus Christ, and him crucified”: that is all Paul taught them. Christ died for your sins; repent and believe on him as your savior.

“In weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling”: they were being persecuted by Rome. “Not with enticing words of man’s wisdom”: not saying things just to make you join, as the church does, “but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power”, the power of teaching about the black Messiah who died to save the 12 tribes of Israel. Christian philosophy, Methodist, Baptist, Catholic, that is the wisdom of men, not God’s plan.
“Not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought”: the ideologies they give you to keep you from God, in debt to them and looking up to them. They come to nothing.

“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery.” People are curious about what we are teaching and why we wear purple and gold; they want to know what is going on in our schools, and it is none of your damn business: Joel Osteen is down the street. Bums from other churches come into our chat at 3 in the morning, when they could be watching Netflix or at the club; low life with no life. It is a mystery to them. “Even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory”: the secrets are given to us for our glory, and we are telling God’s story.
“Ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God”: that is who we are, declaring the mysteries of God. “It is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.”

“Who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts”: some of you are hiding things, but the Lord will make known the hidden things of the heart.

“That ye might learn in us not to think of men above that which is written, that no one of you be puffed up for one against another.” Some take these secrets and their understanding and think they are better than each other. It is easy to look at a man who knows the mysteries as if he is so great. We are to be humble with each other; come humble and to learn, and we match your energy, but come with arrogance and you get that work. In this ministry every state has men known for the scriptures, not one man doing every debate. A camp that only lets one man speak is weak, and Paul was against that.

“For who maketh thee to differ from another? and what hast thou that thou didst not receive?” “I would to God ye did reign, that we also might reign with you”: when you do good, we do good. These mysteries have been given to all of us, and we are all on the same level. If I don’t know something, I’ll tell you.

“O house of Jacob, which are called by the name of Israel”, then “but not in truth, nor in righteousness.” “I have declared the former things from the beginning”, then “I did them suddenly, and they came to pass”: what is written came to pass, through prophecy. That is what we look at, because we are a prophetic ministry.

“Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass”: God knows how we are. So he declared it before it came to pass, “lest thou shouldest say, Mine idol hath done them”: we will give credit to another god, like people who listen to us but won’t leave their ministry, and act like they already knew what we showed them.

“I have shewed thee new things from this time, even hidden things, and thou didst not know them.” You knew nothing of the Israelites, Passover, or the feast of tabernacles coming in October. No black people were going into tents to camp around a fire and talk about God, or into a Saturday sabbath with fringes, their women in skirts, saying shalom. These were secret things the Lord showed us, and look how our lives changed.

“Lest thou shouldest say, Behold, I knew them”: that is how black people are. I always knew I was an Israelite; I always knew Christ was black. Sit your ass down: you didn’t know until you saw us bring it out with the books. Give God the glory. “Yea, thou heardest not; yea, thou knewest not”: you never knew until the Lord revealed his secret to us. Now people look at men with beards and fringes as weird, but the Lord revealed it: fringes and a border of blue, women in skirts and head wraps, praying to the east, no unclean food, no Christmas tree.

“For I knew that thou wouldest deal very treacherously, and wast called a transgressor from the womb.”

“For my name’s sake will I defer mine anger”, then “I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction.” He chose us while we were getting our ass kicked. The furnace of affliction is this captivity, and in it he is refining us, still revealing his secrets to us and raising us up to be a great nation, “for mine own sake.”
“I am the first, I also am the last. Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth”: we have to give God the glory as we bring forth this story and he reveals these secrets to us.

“Which among them hath declared these things?” Nobody ever told us what we know now. “He will do his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans”: he is speaking of America. He is making his name known to us and bringing us our glory in the furnace of affliction, and he will destroy America.

“Thus saith the Lord, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel”: that is who this Bible and these secrets are for, to redeem the Israelites. “Which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go”: we were on the wrong path, and now he leads us the way we need to go.

“O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments!” He told us that from the beginning, when he brought us into a covenant. “Then had thy peace been as a river”: we would be in peace right now, and our seed as the sand.

“Go ye forth of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans, with a voice of singing declare ye, tell this, utter it even to the end of the earth”: which is what we are doing with the secret given to us. We are the Israelites in captivity, and the Lord wants us to utter it to the ends of the earth: “The Lord hath redeemed his servant Jacob.”
